aligned_passages.text: ### 12.3 Relating the two statements The support and scalar models encode closely related control problems. A direct formal application still needs a specified map of their objects. The following contract identifies the obligations, rather than asserting an equivalence of their complete interfaces. **Coefficients.** Restrict the scalar real-time coefficient to $[0,1)$; conversely, choose an extension compatible with the scalar right-continuity predicate. Prove equality almost everywhere of the coefficients used by each payoff and penalty. The scalar endpoint and exterior values are unconstrained by the shape conditions, so two extensions need not be literally equal. **Brownian space.** Bundle or unbundle the same sample space, sigma algebra, probability law and Brownian process. Identify the natural filtration and every elapsed-increment filtration. Equality in law alone does not identify admissible controls on a chosen space. **Controls and payoffs.** Bundle an admissible scalar control as a support control and conversely. With $s=t+r$, prove equality between the absolute integral over $[t,1]$ using $\alpha(s-t)$ and the elapsed integral over $[0,1-t]$ using $\alpha(r)$. Preserve progressive measurability and the pointwise bound $|\alpha|\le1$. **Value and minimizer.** Equality of the payoff sets gives equality of their suprema for every $x$ and $0\le t<1$. Only then identify the first and second spatial derivatives and the Parisi penalties. Transport minimality against every admissible competitor, including restriction or extension of that competitor. **Diffusion and moments.** Reindex the same process between nonnegative and real time, and stop it at one where required. Transport the integral equation on one full-measure event for all $t\in[0,1]$, path continuity, initial value, gradient and moment integrals. The diffusion comparison has a version issue. The support predicate asks for a globally progressive process; the scalar predicate asks for adaptedness of the stopped process and almost-sure continuity on $[0,1]$. There is a concrete ordinary construction of the needed progressive version. For $t\ge0$ and $k=0,1,\ldots$, put $$ X_t^{(k)}=X_{\min(2^{-k}\lfloor2^k t\rfloor,1)}. $$ Each left-step process is progressive: on every bounded time interval, its value on a step is measurable at that step's left endpoint. Define $\bar X_t$ as the pointwise limit where the sequence converges, and zero elsewhere. The convergence set and this limit are progressively measurable. On the single event where $X$ is continuous on $[0,1]$, the equality $\bar X_t=X_{\min(t,1)}$ holds for every $t\ge0$. Thus stopping and reindexing preserve paths, time integrals and moments on that event; no completion of the natural filtration is needed merely to construct this version. The initial value follows from the scalar equation at zero and $B_0=0$ on their common full-measure event. This settles the version construction at the ordinary mathematical level. Its implementation in the two formal predicates, and the coefficient, filtration and value identifications listed above, remain separate obligations. In particular, equality of values for every $x$ is needed before transporting their derivatives; agreement at $(0,0)$ is insufficient. Once those obligations are proved, an application must use the same transported minimizer and associated diffusion in all premises. No such cross-model transport theorem is supplied here. The manuscript proof in §§3–7 and the scalar implementation's independent argument remain available without it. These distinctions come from the defining [support model][support-model] and [scalar model][value-model], rather than from their endpoint names.

The full-support theorem and scalar-value theorem use related but
different formal representations. Their mathematical conclusions can be
discussed together, but a direct formal implication would require the
coefficient, Brownian law, control value and diffusion translations
described in §12, with common witnesses. The finite Gaussian result
also needs its rooted energy identification before it says anything
about a QAOA circuit. The boundedness, regularization, synthesis and
transfer estimates in §8 are additional steps, with temperature-specific
hypotheses where the positive-temperature route is used.

Infinite support allows gaps. An indefinite curvature identity does not imply
strict convexity before expectation is controlled. An algebraic certificate
does not establish its analytic hypotheses. Coordinatewise convergence does
not control a growing coefficient sum. A finite-dimensional Gaussian law
does not identify an energy observable without its operator argument.
Separate witnesses cannot be merged silently. The order
$\forall\varepsilon\ \exists\text{finite word}\ \lim_{n\to\infty}$
cannot be replaced by a fixed-instance depth limit.

The local comparison in §11.1 concerns two printed finite-step displays;
it neither replaces the cited theorem's hypotheses nor supplies the
remaining circuit estimates.

This AI-assisted article reconstructs the cited analytic arguments. The integrated estimate (5), its shape hypotheses and compact-strip approximation are substantial imported inputs. OpenAI's retained [full-support formal statement][support-challenge] asserts the support and moment conclusions conditional on an admissible minimiser, and constructs its associated diffusion. A separate [scalar formal statement][value-challenge] covers value identities and finite Gaussian approximation, with minimiser and diffusion premises for those clauses. Its third clause identifies the ground-state and Parisi values from a minimiser, constructing the diffusion internally. The two formal models have not been transported into one another in this record. Neither statement includes the positive-density corollary or QAOA convergence. Their [full-support][support-lean] and [scalar][value-lean] implementations use [Lean][Lean4] and [mathlib][mathlib]. A source-bound local build of the Support implementation completed on 26 October 2026, and dependency extraction recorded its conditional full-support root. Dependencies outside the selected extraction scope remain boundaries. Comparator acceptance and the scalar-target results remain pending. Exact versions, checking outcomes and correspondence are retained in the long record's [§12, “What the formal statements establish”](../long/reasoning-record.md#formal-interfaces) and [§13, “Source checks and finite calculation”](../long/reasoning-record.md#verification).
